\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{دانشکده} (dâneshkade)}{دانشکده (dâneshkade)}]{\fa{دانشکده} (dâneshkade) — a faculty, a college}

\label{lesson:FA-C400-daneshkade}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to fail, then the Persian for a grade average.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{دانشکده}}
\textbf{\fa{دانشکده}} (\emph{dâneshkade}) — \textquotedblleft{}a faculty, a college\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{دانشکده} \fa{پزشکی} \fa{نزدیک} \fa{بیمارستان} \fa{است}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{dâneshkade-ye pezeshki nazdik-e bimârestân ast.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The medical faculty is near the hospital.
\end{quote}

\emph{Dânesh} \textquotedblleft{}knowledge\textquotedblright{} + \emph{kade} \textquotedblleft{}house\textquotedblright{}. A university has several \emph{dâneshkade}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{دانشکده}} is a native Persian compound built from \emph{dânesh} \textquotedblleft{}knowledge\textquotedblright{}, from \emph{dânestan} \textquotedblleft{}to know\textquotedblright{}, + \emph{kade} \textquotedblleft{}house, dwelling\textquotedblright{}. A faculty is a house of knowledge.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dâneshkade}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dâneshkade}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{dâneshkade}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to fail, then the Persian for a grade average, then say \emph{dâneshkade} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \fa{دانشکده} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A faculty, a college\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{شهریه} (shahriye)}{شهریه (shahriye)}]{\fa{شهریه} (shahriye) — tuition fees}

\label{lesson:FA-C400-shahriye}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a grade average, then the Persian for a faculty.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{شهریه}}
\textbf{\fa{شهریه}} (\emph{shahriye}) — \textquotedblleft{}tuition fees\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{شهریه} \fa{این} \fa{دانشگاه} \fa{گران} \fa{است}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{shahriye-ye in dâneshgâh gerân ast.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The fees at this university are high.
\end{quote}

Also the monthly fee for a private class or a kindergarten.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{شهریه}} is usually traced to Arabic \emph{shahriyya} \textquotedblleft{}monthly\textquotedblright{}, from Arabic \emph{shahr} \textquotedblleft{}month\textquotedblright{} (a different word from Persian \emph{shahr} \textquotedblleft{}city\textquotedblright{}): a fee once paid by the month.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for a grade average, then the Persian for a faculty, then say \emph{shahriye} again

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{پذیرفته} \fa{شدن} (pazirofte shodan)}{پذیرفته شدن (pazirofte shodan)}]{\fa{پذیرفته} \fa{شدن} (pazirofte shodan) — to be admitted, to be accepted}

\label{lesson:FA-C400-pazirofte-shodan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a faculty, then the Persian for tuition fees.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{پذیرفته} \fa{شدن}}
\textbf{\fa{پذیرفته} \fa{شدن}} (\emph{pazirofte shodan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to be admitted, to be accepted\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{او} \fa{در} \fa{رشته} \fa{پزشکی} \fa{پذیرفته} \fa{شد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{u dar reshte-ye pezeshki pazirofte shod.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
She was admitted to study medicine.
\end{quote}

\emph{Pazirofte}, the participle of \emph{paziroftan} \textquotedblleft{}to accept\textquotedblright{} (present stem \emph{pazir-}), + \emph{shodan}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{پذیرفته} \fa{شدن}} is native Persian, built from \emph{pazirofte}, the participle of \emph{paziroftan} \textquotedblleft{}to accept\textquotedblright{}, which EtymDB traces to Middle Persian, and \emph{shodan} \textquotedblleft{}to become\textquotedblright{}, which makes it passive.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for a faculty, then the Persian for tuition fees, then say \emph{pazirofte shodan} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{بورسیه} (bursiye)}{بورسیه (bursiye)}]{\fa{بورسیه} (bursiye) — a scholarship}

\label{lesson:FA-C400-bursiye}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for tuition fees, then the Persian for to be admitted.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{بورسیه}}
\textbf{\fa{بورسیه}} (\emph{bursiye}) — \textquotedblleft{}a scholarship\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{او} \fa{با} \fa{بورسیه} \fa{به} \fa{خارج} \fa{رفت}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{u bâ bursiye be khârej raft.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
She went abroad on a scholarship.
\end{quote}

\emph{Bursiye gereftan} — to win a scholarship.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{بورسیه}} is usually traced to French \emph{bourse} \textquotedblleft{}purse; grant\textquotedblright{}, from Late Latin \emph{bursa} \textquotedblleft{}purse\textquotedblright{}, with the ending \emph{-iye}: money put in a student's purse.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{واحد} (vâhed)}{واحد (vâhed)}]{\fa{واحد} (vâhed) — a course credit; a unit}

\label{lesson:FA-C400-vahed}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to be admitted, then the Persian for a scholarship.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{واحد}}
\textbf{\fa{واحد}} (\emph{vâhed}) — \textquotedblleft{}a course credit; a unit\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{این} \fa{ترم} \fa{بیست} \fa{واحد} \fa{گرفتم}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{in term bist vâhed gereftam.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
This term I took twenty credits.
\end{quote}

Also a unit of measure, and a flat in a building. Its first meaning is \textquotedblleft{}one\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{واحد}} is usually traced to Arabic \emph{wāḥid} \textquotedblleft{}one\textquotedblright{}: a unit is one of something.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
